summary: Layer R03.6 develops the commutative algebra with which a patching argument concludes. It introduces nearly faithful modules in the radical form Ann_R(M) ⊆ √0, which agrees with Taylor's nilpotent form over Noetherian rings and is characterised for finite modules by full support, and modules supported on a union of irreducible components. Supports are transported along arbitrary base change of finite modules and flat base change of arbitrary modules, along surjections, through coefficient changes and through the removal of framing variables; minimal primes and near faithfulness are compared before and after inverting a nonzerodivisor ϖ. A nonzero module of maximal depth over a Noetherian local ring is supported on top-dimensional components but need not be nearly faithful; it is nearly faithful when the ring has one minimal prime, and near faithfulness then forces equidimensionality. Near faithfulness spreads along a group acting transitively on components and lifts from the special fibre under Taylor's catenarity hypotheses. For the patched module of layer R03.5 these results give the Calegari–Geraghty conclusions: near faithfulness of H over R and (R∞/𝔞)_red ≅ R_red, or, over a regular R∞, freeness and ker φ∞ = 𝔞R∞. Three R = T theorems close the layer: R_red ≅ T exactly when T is reduced, R^tf ≅ T exactly when H[1/ϖ] is faithful, and R ≅ T exactly when H is faithful.

nodes.title: Nearly faithful modules
nodes.statement: Let R be a commutative ring and M an R-module. M is nearly faithful over R if Ann_R(M) ⊆ nilradical(R), that is, every element of R that kills M is nilpotent; equivalently √Ann_R(M) = √0. The definition carries no Noetherian or finiteness hypothesis. Characterisations, each an item of the API: (a) if Ann_R(M) is finitely generated, in particular if R is Noetherian, M is nearly faithful iff Ann_R(M) is a nilpotent ideal (Taylor's Definition 2.1); (b) if every minimal prime of R lies in Supp_R(M), M is nearly faithful, for every M; if M is finite, M is nearly faithful iff Supp_R(M) = Spec R iff every minimal prime of R lies in Supp_R(M) (the lemma nearly-faithful-iff-support-eq-univ); (c) a faithful module is nearly faithful; (d) if R is reduced, M is nearly faithful iff M is faithful.
hypotheses: R commutative; M an arbitrary R-module.
(a) needs Ann_R(M) finitely generated, which holds when R is Noetherian; without it the nilpotent form is strictly stronger (Stacks Example 0EGG).
(b) needs M finite for 'nearly faithful ⇒ Supp M = Spec R'; 'every minimal prime in Supp M ⇒ nearly faithful' holds for every M.
(d) needs R reduced.
proofSteps: (a) A nilpotent ideal lies in √0, with no hypothesis. Conversely, if Ann_R(M) ⊆ √0 and Ann_R(M) is finitely generated, then Ann_R(M)^n = 0 for some n (Stacks 00IM; Mathlib Ideal.FG.isNilpotent_iff_le_nilradical). Over a Noetherian ring every ideal is finitely generated.

(b), the implication for every M: if 𝔭 ∈ Supp M then some m ∈ M has Ann(m) ⊆ 𝔭 (Mathlib Module.mem_support_iff_exists_annihilator), so Ann M ⊆ 𝔭. If every minimal prime lies in Supp M, then Ann M ⊆ ⋂ Min(R) = √0 (Mathlib Ideal.sInf_minimalPrimes for the zero ideal).
(b), the implication for finite M: Supp M = V(Ann M) (Stacks 00L2; Mathlib Module.support_eq_zeroLocus), and V(I) = Spec R iff I ⊆ √0 (Mathlib PrimeSpectrum.zeroLocus_eq_univ_iff).
(c) Faithful means Ann_R(M) = 0 (Mathlib Module.annihilator_eq_bot). (d) √0 = 0 when R is reduced (Mathlib nilradical_eq_bot_iff).

Functoriality: an injective linear map M → N gives Ann N ⊆ Ann M (Mathlib LinearMap.annihilator_le_of_injective), and linear equivalences preserve annihilators (Mathlib LinearEquiv.annihilator_eq). Over a nonzero ring a nearly faithful module is nonzero, because Ann(0) = R (Mathlib Module.annihilator_eq_top_iff) and 1 is not nilpotent.
acceptance: Over the dual numbers k[ε], the module k = k[ε]/(ε) is nearly faithful and not faithful.

In S = k[x_0, x_1, …]/(x_n^{n+1} : n ≥ 0) with J = (x_n : n ≥ 0), the S-module S/J is nearly faithful (J ⊆ √0), although Ann_S(S/J) = J is not nilpotent (Stacks Example 0EGG). This separates the definition from Taylor's nilpotent form outside the finitely generated case.
Over the node A = k[[x,y]]/(xy), the module A/(x) is not nearly faithful: its support V(x) misses the component V(y).
Over a nonzero ring the zero module is not nearly faithful.

nodes.title: Modules supported on a union of irreducible components
nodes.statement: Let R be a commutative ring and M an R-module. M is supported on components of Spec R if every prime minimal over Ann_R(M) is a minimal prime of R. For finite M this says exactly that Supp_R(M), which equals the closed set V(Ann_R M), is a union of irreducible components of Spec R, namely Supp M = ⋃_{𝔭 ∈ Min(R) ∩ Supp M} V(𝔭). The notion is used for finite modules; for a module that is not finite Supp M can differ from V(Ann M). A nearly faithful module is supported on components, all of them occurring.
hypotheses: R commutative.
The characterisation by irreducible components needs M finite, so that Supp M = V(Ann M) (Stacks 00L2).
proofSteps: Characterisation, ⇒: every prime containing Ann M contains a prime minimal over Ann M (Stacks 00E0; Mathlib Ideal.exists_minimalPrimes_le), which is a minimal prime Q of R by hypothesis; so V(Ann M) = ⋃ V(Q) over these Q, and V(Q) is an irreducible component (Mathlib minimalPrimes.equivIrreducibleComponents).

Characterisation, ⇐: if Supp M = ⋃ V(Q_j) with Q_j minimal in R and 𝔭 is minimal over Ann M, then 𝔭 ∈ V(Ann M) = Supp M (Mathlib Module.support_eq_zeroLocus) gives 𝔭 ⊇ Q_j ⊇ Ann M for some j, so 𝔭 = Q_j by minimality.
Relation to nearly-faithful: if Ann M ⊆ √0, every prime contains Ann M, so the primes minimal over Ann M are the minimal primes of R.
acceptance: Over ℤ, the module ℤ/2 is not supported on components: (2) is minimal over Ann = (2) and is not a minimal prime of ℤ.
Over the node A = k[[x,y]]/(xy), A/(x) is supported on components (Supp = V(x), one component) and is not nearly faithful.

Finiteness is needed for the characterisation: over ℤ_p, M = ℚ_p/ℤ_p has Ann M = 0, so the only prime minimal over Ann M is the minimal prime (0), yet Supp M = {(p)} is not a union of irreducible components.

nodes.title: Near faithfulness as full support
nodes.statement: Let R be a commutative ring and M an R-module, and consider (i) M is nearly faithful; (ii) Supp_R M = Spec R; (iii) every minimal prime of R lies in Supp_R M. For every M, (ii) ⇔ (iii) ⇒ (i). If M is finite, (i), (ii) and (iii) are equivalent. If moreover Ann_R M is finitely generated (for instance R Noetherian), they are equivalent to (iv) Ann_R M is a nilpotent ideal.
hypotheses: M finite for (i) ⇒ (ii); the other implications among (i)–(iii) hold for every M.
Ann_R M finitely generated, automatic for R Noetherian, for (iv).

(ii) ⇔ (iii): every prime contains a minimal prime (Stacks 00E0; Mathlib Ideal.exists_minimalPrimes_le) and supports are stable under specialisation (Mathlib Module.mem_support_mono).
(i) ⇒ (ii) for finite M: Supp M = V(Ann M) (Stacks 00L2; Mathlib Module.support_eq_zeroLocus) and V(I) = Spec R iff I ⊆ √0 (Mathlib PrimeSpectrum.zeroLocus_eq_univ_iff).

nodes.title: Near faithfulness along a surjective ring map
nodes.statement: Let φ: A → B be a surjective ring map and N a B-module, viewed as an A-module through φ. Then Ann_A(N) = φ⁻¹(Ann_B N), and N is nearly faithful over B iff Ann_A(N) ⊆ √(ker φ). In particular, if N is nearly faithful over A, then ker φ ⊆ √0_A and N is nearly faithful over B.
hypotheses: φ surjective.
No finiteness of N and no Noetherian hypothesis.
proofSteps: Ann_A(N) = φ⁻¹(Ann_B N) (Mathlib Module.comap_annihilator).
φ⁻¹(√0_B) = √(φ⁻¹(0)) = √(ker φ) (Mathlib Ideal.comap_radical).
As φ is surjective, Ann_B N = φ(Ann_A N); so Ann_B N ⊆ √0_B iff Ann_A N ⊆ φ⁻¹(√0_B) = √(ker φ).
If Ann_A N ⊆ √0_A, then ker φ ⊆ Ann_A N ⊆ √0_A ⊆ √(ker φ).
acceptance: For B = A/I and N = A/J with I ⊆ J: A/J is nearly faithful over A/I iff J ⊆ √I.
A/I is faithful over A/I, and nearly faithful over A iff I ⊆ √0.

nodes.title: Near faithfulness passes to quotients
nodes.statement: Let A be a commutative ring, M a finite nearly faithful A-module and I ⊆ A an ideal. Then M/IM is nearly faithful over A/I. Moreover, let φ: A → B be a surjective ring map and N a B-module with an A-linear isomorphism M/IM ≅ N (the action of A on M/IM factors through B = A/J, J = ker φ). Then J ⊆ √I; and if I ⊆ √J (for instance I ⊆ J), N is nearly faithful over B.
hypotheses: M finite over A.
No Noetherian hypothesis.
proofSteps: Supp_A(M/IM) = Supp_A M ∩ V(I) (Stacks 00L3; Mathlib Module.support_quotient) = V(I), because Supp_A M = Spec A (nearly-faithful-iff-support-eq-univ).
M/IM is finite, so V(Ann_A(M/IM)) = Supp_A(M/IM) = V(I) (Mathlib Module.support_eq_zeroLocus), whence √Ann_A(M/IM) = √I (Mathlib PrimeSpectrum.zeroLocus_subset_zeroLocus_iff).

The A/I-module structure on M/IM is Mathlib's (Module.isTorsionBySet_quotient_ideal_smul and Module.IsTorsionBySet.module). By nearly-faithful-restrict-scalars-surjective for A → A/I, M/IM is nearly faithful over A/I iff Ann_A(M/IM) ⊆ √I, which holds.
For B: J kills N ≅ M/IM, so J ⊆ Ann_A(M/IM) ⊆ √I. If I ⊆ √J, then Ann_A(N) ⊆ √I ⊆ √J, and nearly-faithful-restrict-scalars-surjective gives N nearly faithful over B.

nodes.title: Support under base change
nodes.statement: Let φ: A → B be a ring map and M an A-module. For every M and every φ, Supp_B(B ⊗_A M) ⊆ (Spec φ)⁻¹(Supp_A M). If M is finite over A, or if φ is flat, equality holds: Supp_B(B ⊗_A M) = (Spec φ)⁻¹(Supp_A M).
hypotheses: φ: A → B a map of commutative rings.
For equality: M finite over A, or φ flat. Equality fails when both are dropped.
proofSteps: For 𝔮 ∈ Spec B with 𝔭 = φ⁻¹(𝔮): (B ⊗_A M)_𝔮 ≅ B_𝔮 ⊗_{A_𝔭} M_𝔭 (proof of Stacks 0BUR). So M_𝔭 = 0 forces (B ⊗_A M)_𝔮 = 0: this is the inclusion ⊆.

⊇ for finite M: M_𝔭 ≠ 0 gives κ(𝔭) ⊗_A M ≠ 0 (Mathlib Module.mem_support_iff_nontrivial_residueField_tensorProduct, Nakayama). Then κ(𝔮) ⊗_B (B ⊗_A M) ≅ κ(𝔮) ⊗_{κ(𝔭)} (κ(𝔭) ⊗_A M) is nonzero, κ(𝔭) → κ(𝔮) being a field extension; apply the same criterion over B, where B ⊗_A M is finite (Mathlib Module.Finite.base_change).
⊇ for flat φ: A_𝔭 → B_𝔮 is a flat local homomorphism of local rings, hence faithfully flat (Stacks 00HR; Mathlib Module.FaithfullyFlat.of_flat_of_isLocalHom), so B_𝔮 ⊗_{A_𝔭} M_𝔭 ≠ 0 when M_𝔭 ≠ 0.

For the flat map A → A[1/ϖ]: Supp_{A[1/ϖ]}(M[1/ϖ]) is Supp_A M ∩ D(ϖ), viewed in Spec A[1/ϖ] = D(ϖ).

nodes.title: Near faithfulness under base change and coefficient change
nodes.statement: Let φ: A → B be a ring map and M a finite A-module. (a) If M is nearly faithful over A, then B ⊗_A M is nearly faithful over B. (b) If B ⊗_A M is nearly faithful over B and every minimal prime of A is φ⁻¹(𝔮) for some prime 𝔮 of B (for instance φ faithfully flat), then M is nearly faithful over A. (c) Coefficient change: if 𝒪 → 𝒪′ is faithfully flat (for instance a finite extension of complete discrete valuation rings) and A is an 𝒪-algebra, then M is nearly faithful over A iff (A ⊗_𝒪 𝒪′) ⊗_A M ≅ 𝒪′ ⊗_𝒪 M is nearly faithful over A ⊗_𝒪 𝒪′.
hypotheses: M finite over A.
(b): every minimal prime of A lies in the image of Spec B → Spec A.
No Noetherian hypothesis.
proofSteps: (a) support-base-change: Supp_B(B ⊗_A M) = (Spec φ)⁻¹(Supp_A M) = (Spec φ)⁻¹(Spec A) = Spec B. B ⊗_A M is B-finite (Mathlib Module.Finite.base_change); conclude by nearly-faithful-iff-support-eq-univ.

(b) A minimal prime 𝔭 equals φ⁻¹(𝔮); 𝔮 ∈ Supp_B(B ⊗_A M) = Spec B (nearly-faithful-iff-support-eq-univ over B), so 𝔭 ∈ Supp_A M by support-base-change; conclude by nearly-faithful-iff-support-eq-univ over A.

(c) A → A ⊗_𝒪 𝒪′ is faithfully flat (Stacks 00HI; the base-change instance of Mathlib's Module.FaithfullyFlat), hence surjective on spectra (Stacks 00HQ; Mathlib PrimeSpectrum.comap_surjective_of_faithfullyFlat). Apply (a) and (b).
acceptance: Descent fails without the hypothesis of (b): A = k × k, B = k by the first projection, M = k × 0 = A/(0 × k). Then B ⊗_A M = k is faithful over B, but Ann_A M = 0 × k ⊄ √0 = 0.

nodes.title: Removing framing variables
nodes.statement: Let A be a commutative ring, σ a finite set and A[[x]] := A[[x_s : s ∈ σ]]. (0) The constant-coefficient map A[[x]] → A has kernel (x_s : s ∈ σ), so A[[x]]/(x) ≅ A. (a) A finite A-module M is nearly faithful over A iff A[[x]] ⊗_A M is nearly faithful over A[[x]]. (b) If N is a finite nearly faithful A[[x]]-module, then N/(x)N is nearly faithful over A = A[[x]]/(x).
hypotheses: σ finite. For infinitely many variables Σ_s x_s has constant coefficient 0 and does not lie in the ideal (x_s : s ∈ σ), so (0) fails.
M finite over A; N finite over A[[x]].
No Noetherian or flatness hypothesis.
proofSteps: (0) Write σ = {s_1, …, s_n}. Every f ∈ A[[x]] equals f(0) + Σ_i x_{s_i} g_i, where x_{s_i} g_i collects the monomials of f whose least occurring variable is x_{s_i}; every non-constant monomial is counted exactly once. So ker(constant coefficient) = (x_s : s ∈ σ).
(b) nearly-faithful-quotient with I = (x_s : s ∈ σ) gives N/(x)N nearly faithful over A[[x]]/(x), which is A by (0).
(a) ⇒ is nearly-faithful-base-change (a).

(a) ⇐: N = A[[x]] ⊗_A M is A[[x]]-finite, and N/(x)N ≅ (A[[x]]/(x)) ⊗_A M ≅ M as A-modules (Mathlib TensorProduct.quotTensorEquivQuotSMul and (0)). Apply (b) and invariance of near faithfulness under linear equivalence (API of nearly-faithful).

nodes.title: Minimal primes after inverting a nonzerodivisor
nodes.statement: Let R be a commutative ring and ϖ ∈ R a nonzerodivisor. Then ϖ lies in no minimal prime of R, and contraction 𝔮 ↦ 𝔮 ∩ R along R → R[1/ϖ] is a bijection from the minimal primes of R[1/ϖ] onto the minimal primes of R, with inverse 𝔭 ↦ 𝔭R[1/ϖ].
hypotheses: ϖ a nonzerodivisor of R. No Noetherian or discrete-valuation hypothesis.
proofSteps: First half: Mathlib Ideal.disjoint_nonZeroDivisors_of_mem_minimalPrimes (an element x of a minimal prime 𝔭 has s xⁿ = 0 for some s ∉ 𝔭, Stacks 00EU).

Mathlib IsLocalization.minimalPrimes_comap with J = 0: the contractions of the minimal primes of R[1/ϖ] are the primes minimal over ker(R → R[1/ϖ]). This kernel is 0 because ϖ is a nonzerodivisor (Mathlib IsLocalization.eq_iff_exists), so they are the minimal primes of R.

Contraction is injective on Spec R[1/ϖ] (Mathlib PrimeSpectrum.localization_comap_injective) with image D(ϖ) (Mathlib PrimeSpectrum.localization_away_comap_range; Stacks 00E3); the inverse is extension.
acceptance: The nonzerodivisor hypothesis is needed: in R = ℤ_p × 𝔽_p with ϖ = (p, 0), the minimal prime ℤ_p × 0 contains ϖ, and R[1/ϖ] = ℚ_p has one minimal prime while R has two.

nodes.title: Near faithfulness tested after inverting ϖ
nodes.statement: Let R be a commutative ring, ϖ ∈ R a nonzerodivisor and M a finite R-module. The following are equivalent: (i) M is nearly faithful over R; (ii) M[1/ϖ] is nearly faithful over R[1/ϖ]; (iii) every irreducible component of Spec R[1/ϖ] lies in Supp M[1/ϖ]. If moreover R[1/ϖ] is reduced (for instance regular), then R is reduced and (i)–(iii) are equivalent to (iv) M is faithful over R and to (v) M[1/ϖ] is faithful over R[1/ϖ].
hypotheses: ϖ a nonzerodivisor of R.
M finite over R.
(iv), (v): R[1/ϖ] reduced.
No Noetherian hypothesis.
proofSteps: M[1/ϖ] ≅ R[1/ϖ] ⊗_R M (Mathlib LocalizedModule.equivTensorProduct). By support-base-change, Supp M[1/ϖ] is the preimage of Supp M, that is Supp M ∩ D(ϖ) inside Spec R (Stacks 00E3).

By minimal-primes-of-torsion-free the minimal primes of R lie in D(ϖ) and are the contractions of the minimal primes of R[1/ϖ]; so Min(R) ⊆ Supp M iff Min(R[1/ϖ]) ⊆ Supp M[1/ϖ]. M[1/ϖ] is finite over R[1/ϖ]; conclude (i) ⇔ (ii) by nearly-faithful-iff-support-eq-univ over R and over R[1/ϖ].

(ii) ⇔ (iii): the irreducible components of Spec R[1/ϖ] are the closures V(𝔮) of its minimal primes (Mathlib minimalPrimes.equivIrreducibleComponents), and V(𝔮) ⊆ Supp iff 𝔮 ∈ Supp (supports are stable under specialisation).

If R[1/ϖ] is reduced, R ↪ R[1/ϖ] (ϖ a nonzerodivisor) makes R reduced (Mathlib isReduced_of_injective); then nearly faithful ⇔ faithful over R and over R[1/ϖ] (API item nearlyFaithful_iff_faithfulSMul of nearly-faithful).

M must be finite: over ℤ_p, M = ℚ_p/ℤ_p is faithful while M[1/p] = 0.

nodes.title: Modules of maximal depth are supported on top-dimensional components
nodes.statement: Let (A, 𝔪) be a Noetherian local ring and M ≠ 0 a finite A-module with depth_A M ≥ dim A (M maximal Cohen–Macaulay). Then depth_A M = dim A; every associated prime 𝔭 of M is a minimal prime of A with dim A/𝔭 = dim A; the primes minimal over Ann_A M are therefore minimal primes of A of maximal dimension; so M is supported on components (supported-on-components) and Supp M is a union of irreducible components of Spec A of dimension dim A. The theorem does not give full support: M need not be nearly faithful.
hypotheses: A Noetherian local.
M finite and nonzero.
depth_A M ≥ dim A.
proofSteps: For 𝔭 ∈ Ass M: depth M ≤ dim A/𝔭 (Stacks 0BK4; layer R03.3). Hence dim A ≤ dim A/𝔭 ≤ dim A, so dim A/𝔭 = dim A; 𝔭 is minimal, since a prime strictly inside 𝔭 would give a chain longer than dim A, which is finite (R03.3).
M ≠ 0 has an associated prime (R03.3); for it, depth M ≤ dim A/𝔭 = dim A, so depth M = dim A.

The primes minimal over Ann M are associated primes of M (Stacks 02CE; Mathlib Module.associatedPrimes.minimalPrimes_annihilator_subset_associatedPrimes), hence minimal primes of A of maximal dimension. This is supported-on-components, and its characterisation makes Supp M a union of irreducible components.
acceptance: A = k[[x,y]]/(xy), M = A/(x) ≅ k[[y]]: x + y is M-regular, so depth_A M = 1 = dim A; Supp M = V(x) is one of the two components, and M is not nearly faithful (Ann M = (x) is not nilpotent).

M = 0 is excluded: depth 0 = ∞ in the Stacks convention (proof of Stacks 0FCC), so the hypothesis holds while 'depth = dim A' fails. Taylor's Lemma 2.3 omits M ≠ 0 (source issue DeformationAndDerivedPatchingAlgebra/E2).

nodes.title: Support stable under a group acting transitively on components
nodes.statement: Let G be a group acting on a commutative ring A by ring automorphisms and on an A-module M by additive bijections with g(a·m) = g(a)·g(m). Then Ann_A(M) is G-stable and Supp_A(M) is stable under 𝔭 ↦ g(𝔭). If G acts transitively on the minimal primes of A and Supp_A(M) contains one minimal prime, then every minimal prime lies in Supp_A(M) and M is nearly faithful; if A is Noetherian, Ann_A(M) is nilpotent; if A is reduced, M is faithful.

nodes.title: Lifting near faithfulness from the special fibre
nodes.statement: Let (A, 𝔪) be a Noetherian local ring and ϖ ∈ 𝔪 (in the source A is an 𝒪-algebra and ϖ = λ is a uniformiser of 𝒪). Assume that A is catenary, which for a Noetherian local ring means that 𝔭 ↦ dim A/𝔭 is a dimension function (dim A/𝔭 = dim A/𝔮 + 1 whenever 𝔮 is an immediate specialisation of 𝔭); that A is equidimensional (dim A/P = dim A for every minimal prime P); that no minimal prime of A contains ϖ (the generic points of Spec A lie over the generic fibre); and that every prime of A minimal over ϖA contains exactly one minimal prime of A. Let M be a finite A-module on which ϖ is a nonzerodivisor. If M/ϖM is nearly faithful over A/ϖA, then M is nearly faithful over A.
hypotheses: A Noetherian local and ϖ ∈ 𝔪.
A catenary (in dimension-function form) and equidimensional.
No minimal prime of A contains ϖ.
Each prime minimal over ϖA contains exactly one minimal prime of A.
M finite, and ϖ a nonzerodivisor on M (M is 𝒪-torsion-free).
proofSteps: Let P be a minimal prime of A. As ϖ ∈ 𝔪, P + ϖA is proper; let ℘ be a prime minimal over it (Mathlib Ideal.exists_minimalPrimes_le). Krull's principal ideal theorem in the domain A/P (Mathlib Ideal.height_le_one_of_isPrincipal_of_mem_minimalPrimes; Stacks 00KV) shows that no prime lies strictly between P and ℘, and P ≠ ℘ because ϖ ∉ P.

The dimension-function hypothesis gives dim A/℘ = dim A/P − 1 = dim A − 1. For a prime 𝔮 ⊊ ℘, dim A/𝔮 ≥ dim A/℘ + 1 = dim A (Mathlib ringKrullDim_quotient), so dim A/𝔮 = dim A and 𝔮 is a minimal prime (dim A is finite; layer R03.3). So ϖ ∉ 𝔮 for every 𝔮 ⊊ ℘, ℘ is minimal over ϖA, P is the only minimal prime inside ℘, and every prime strictly inside ℘ equals P.

M/ϖM is finite and nearly faithful over A/ϖA, so Ann_A(M/ϖM) ⊆ √(ϖA) (nearly-faithful-restrict-scalars-surjective) and ℘ ∈ V(ϖA) ⊆ Supp_A(M/ϖM) (Mathlib Module.support_eq_zeroLocus). Since Supp_A(M/ϖM) = Supp M ∩ V(ϖ) (Mathlib Module.support_quotient), ℘ ∈ Supp M, i.e. Ann M ⊆ ℘.

Choose 𝔮 ⊆ ℘ minimal over Ann M (Mathlib Ideal.exists_minimalPrimes_le). As ϖ is M-regular, ϖ ∉ 𝔮 (Mathlib IsSMulRegular.notMem_of_mem_minimalPrimes), so 𝔮 ≠ ℘ and 𝔮 = P by the second step. Hence Ann M ⊆ P and P ∈ Supp M (Mathlib Module.mem_support_iff_of_finite). As P was arbitrary, nearly-faithful-iff-support-eq-univ concludes.
acceptance: ϖ-torsion-freeness of M is needed: A = ℤ_p, ϖ = p, M = 𝔽_p satisfy every other hypothesis and M/pM = 𝔽_p is nearly faithful over 𝔽_p, but M is not nearly faithful over ℤ_p.

The uniqueness hypothesis is needed: A = ℤ_p[[x]]/(x(x − p)) is complete, equidimensional of dimension 1, with minimal primes (x) and (x − p), neither containing p, both inside ℘ = (p, x). M = A/(x) ≅ ℤ_p is p-torsion-free, and M/pM = 𝔽_p is nearly faithful over A/pA = 𝔽_p[[x]]/(x²), but M is not nearly faithful over A.

If M∞ is nearly faithful over R∞, then √(ı(𝔞)R∞) = √(ker φ); hence (R∞/ı(𝔞)R∞)_red ≅ R_red compatibly with the maps from R∞, and H is nearly faithful over R∞/ı(𝔞)R∞ and over R.

nodes.statement: In the setting of patching-nearly-faithful-descends (ı: S → R∞, 𝔞, φ: R∞ ↠ R, M∞ finite, H ≅ M∞/ı(𝔞)M∞ an R-module through φ, and (b) ı(𝔞) ⊆ ker φ + Ann_{R∞}(M∞)), assume that R∞ is a regular local ring and that M∞ ≠ 0 with depth_{R∞} M∞ ≥ dim R∞. nodes.title: Reduced R = T from near faithfulness

nodes.title: Torsion-free R = T
nodes.statement: Let R be a commutative ring, ϖ ∈ R, H an R-module on which ϖ is a nonzerodivisor, and T a commutative R-algebra acting faithfully on H, compatibly with R, with R → T surjective (for instance the image of R in End(H)). Let R[ϖ^∞] = ker(R → R[1/ϖ]) be the ϖ-power torsion ideal and R^tf := R/R[ϖ^∞]. (a) R[ϖ^∞] ⊆ Ann_R(H), so R → T factors through R^tf, and ϖ is a nonzerodivisor on T. (b) Ann_{R[1/ϖ]}(H[1/ϖ]) = Ann_R(H)[1/ϖ]; hence H[1/ϖ] is faithful over R[1/ϖ] iff ker(R → T) = R[ϖ^∞] iff R^tf → T is an isomorphism ('R = T up to ϖ-torsion'). (c) If H is nearly faithful, then R[ϖ^∞] ⊆ √0, (R^tf)_red = R_red ≅ T_red, and T is reduced iff T[1/ϖ] is reduced, in which case R_red ≅ T (r-equals-t-reduced).

(b) H ↪ H[1/ϖ], so r/ϖᵏ kills H[1/ϖ] iff r kills H (Mathlib IsLocalization.eq_iff_exists and ϖ-regularity). Hence H[1/ϖ] is faithful iff Ann_R(H) ⊆ R[ϖ^∞] (Mathlib Module.annihilator_eq_bot); with (a) this means Ann_R(H) = R[ϖ^∞], and Ann_R(H) = ker(R → T) as in r-equals-t-reduced.

nodes.title: Integral R = T from faithfulness
nodes.statement: Let R be a commutative ring, H an R-module and T a commutative R-algebra acting faithfully on H, compatibly with R, with R → T surjective (for instance T = the image of R in End(H)). Then R → T is an isomorphism iff H is faithful over R. In particular, if H is free of positive rank over R (for instance by patching-free-conclusion), then R ≅ T integrally.
hypotheses: T acts faithfully on H through R → T, which is surjective.
H faithful over R. Freeness of positive rank suffices; freeness alone does not (the zero module is free).
proofSteps: ker(R → T) = Ann_R(H) (Mathlib Module.comap_annihilator, T acting faithfully); so R → T is injective iff Ann_R(H) = 0 iff H is faithful (Mathlib Module.annihilator_eq_bot).
A free module with a basis vector b is faithful: r ↦ r·b is injective (Mathlib Module.Free.chooseBasis).
acceptance: The zero module is free over ℤ and not faithful: freeness alone does not give R ≅ T.
Calegari–Geraghty, Theorem 6.4(1): R acts freely on H ≠ 0, so R maps isomorphically to its image in End(H).

nodes.title: Support and faithfulness of the patched module
nodes.statement: Let M∞ be a patched module as constructed in layer R03.5: a finite module over a complete Noetherian local 𝒪-algebra R∞, with a ring map ı: S∞ → R∞ from the patching algebra, its augmentation ideal 𝔞 (which contains the framing variables), a surjection φ∞: R∞ ↠ R, an R-module H ≠ 0 and an R∞-linear isomorphism M∞/𝔞M∞ ≅ H with R∞ acting on H through φ∞, such that the image of 𝔞 in End(M∞) lies in the image of ker φ∞, and with depth_{R∞} M∞ = dim R∞. Then: (0) Supp_{R∞} M∞ is a union of irreducible components of Spec R∞ of dimension dim R∞, and if M∞ is nearly faithful, R∞ is equidimensional; (1) if R∞ is regular (formally smooth over 𝒪), then ker φ∞ = ı(𝔞)R∞, H is free of positive rank over R, and R → T is an isomorphism for every ring T through which R acts faithfully on H, in particular for the image of R in End(H); (2) if R∞ has a unique minimal prime (in particular if ϖ is a nonzerodivisor of R∞ and Spec R∞[1/ϖ] is irreducible), then H is nearly faithful over R and (R∞/ı(𝔞)R∞)_red ≅ R_red; (3) if ϖ is a nonzerodivisor of R∞ and every irreducible component of Spec R∞[1/ϖ] lies in Supp M∞[1/ϖ], the conclusions of (2) hold.

H ≠ 0, hence M∞ ≠ 0.
